The new traces show the context guard still sees `[sched] stack watch armed thread=startup … suspect=0x0000000000000000`, so we were blindly re‑using the default stack watch slot instead of re-arming it with the guard’s diff address.

`thread_stack_watch_activate` now forcefully re-arms the watch even when it was already active: whenever we get another context-guard mismatch, we first deactivate the old guard and then arm it again with the new context + suspect pointer. Because arming always captures a fresh snapshot, the watchdog can now catch an actual delta at the address the guard complained about, instead of sitting forever on whatever suspect happened to be stored at boot.

This should give you suspects like `suspect=0x000000000235CFC0` in the arm log and, if the DMA/CPU scribbler fires again, the “[sched] stack watch delta … addr=… old=… new=…” you saw earlier. Rebuild (`make -j8`) succeeded; please boot again (`make run-hdd`) and check whether the next mismatch produces a delta rather than a release loop.
